structure: Part 19 read, in full, everything repos/trade-imports-animals-frontend keeps as a recorded decision rather than as code: the platform ledgers under src/server/app/docs/ (decisions.md, 8 architecture-decision headings; README.md, the four-layer composition note; flow-and-gates.md, 166 lines of flow, gate, navigation and trail rules; limits.md, 5 platform limits; obligation-model.md, the model contract and the gate-helper choice rules), the live-animals set's own records under src/server/app/sets/live-animals/docs/ (README.md index, page-design.md's 788-line per-page design-decision record under its 15 headings Overview (hub), How a page ends, Check your answers (review), Submitted page, Declaration, Origin of the import, Main import reason, Additional details, Identification, Commodity pages, Consignment addresses pages, CPH number, Permanent address, Documents and Transport, journey-flow-and-gates.md's 297 lines of section order, task rows, declaration concurrency, entry guard, Back table, check-your-answers Back, registration wiring and section captions, features.md's feature anatomy and page-maturity levels, limits.md's set caps, obligation-model.md's set manifest and allow-list checks, and copy-status.md's unreviewed Welsh copy), plus AGENTS.md and README.md at the repo root. It claims the recorded decisions, rulings, limits, maturity levels and copy statuses those files hold, with each claim attributed to its file, line and heading; page behaviour itself is the feature parts' to claim from the code. Verifications run against the code for the ledger statements most likely to have drifted (the hub's six numbered section headings, flow.js's eight sections, the documents cap of fifteen, MAX_FILE_SIZE_MB, the thirteen Welsh document-type labels, the In progress row status) found the ledgers accurate; two stale records are recorded as gaps (README.md's workspace repo URL and page-design.md's .claude/rules/gds.md path), and a third gap records that copy-status.md names no maturity level, the four levels being recorded in features.md instead.

claims.statement: The platform's recorded architecture decision is that a page descriptor's id, slug and page-owned collects are the one identity used by dispatch, gates and navigation, and that page.js stays import-free to avoid cycles.
claims.quote:
A page descriptor has an `id`, a `slug` and page-owned `collects`. The same identity
is used by dispatch, gates and navigation. Controllers and the journey flow import
the descriptor; `page.js` stays import-free to avoid cycles.

policy through explicit configuration seams.

claims.statement: The platform's recorded decision is that the obligation evaluator decides what is in scope and whether it is mandatory or optional, journey sections decide page order and task rows decide how work is grouped on a hub, so another journey style can reuse the same obligation set.

The obligation evaluator decides what is in scope and whether it is mandatory or
optional. Journey sections decide page order. Task rows decide how work is grouped
on a hub. Keeping these facts separate allows another journey style to reuse the
same obligation set.

claims.statement: The platform records that the reachability prover builds a witness for a complement gate from a stable sentinel string outside the gate's derived union, and reports the gate opaque rather than vacuously green if the union held the sentinel and its fallback, because a gate no input can open is an authoring defect.

the gate opaque instead of vacuously green, because a gate no input can open is an
authoring defect. A commodity-code union covers a handful of codes, so any other
string opens the gate.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that a draft is headed by its reference, a Draft tag and the date created, in place of the review heading and status bar, its header offering Copy as new then a red Delete and an Import reference numbers section as for a submitted notification, while it keeps its Change links, error summary and Continue; an amendment keeps the review heading and status bar.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the view of a notification that cannot be found shows the service's standard page not found.

The means of transport row reads the arrival page's own label for the

An answer the reference data has since retired is named on the review with

claims.statement: The page-design record states that a party never answered raises no address error on the review and its card is simply unfinished.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the main-import-reason card carries the exit answers and its one Change link reaches the page that collects them.
claims.quote:
The main-import-reason card carries the exit answers, and its one Change

claims.statement: The page-design record states that a summary entry for a review card that is out of scope is absent, so every entry links to an anchor the page carries.

A summary entry for a card that is out of scope is absent, so every entry

claims.statement: The page-design record states that each review card's Change link ends, for screen readers, with the card's title in lower-case words.
claims.quote:
Each card's Change link ends, for screen readers, with the card's title in
  lower-case words.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the review's form ends with one button group and no heading or sentence stands above it, the group being Continue alone on a draft with its Delete in the header, and Continue, a secondary Cancel amend then a red Delete while amending.
claims.quote:
The review's form ends with one button group, and no heading or sentence

claims.statement: The page-design record states that an unfinished card's line is the same in the error summary and in the card, so a trader reading either sees the same words.

An unfinished card's line is the same in the error summary and in the card,

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the submitted page goes from the reference panel straight to what the trader still owes, and that the declaration date is shown only on the declaration page.

The page goes from the reference panel straight to what the trader still

claims.statement: The page-design record states that documents are not required to submit, and that the submitted page lists the ITAHC as still owed unless an ITAHC is among the journey's documents, whatever its scan state.

Documents are not required to submit. The page lists the ITAHC as still owed
  unless an ITAHC is among the journey's documents, whatever its scan state.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that after the ITAHC item the submitted page lists "complete the animal identifier information in the notification" when a line whose species asks for identifiers holds fewer identified animals than it declares, one filled identifier identifying an animal.
claims.quote:
After the ITAHC item, the page lists "complete the animal identifier
  information in the notification" when a line whose species asks for
  identifiers holds fewer identified animals than it declares. One filled
  identifier identifies an animal.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the submitted page's help links to HMRC open in a new tab, their visible text unchanged and a visually hidden "(opens in a new tab)" telling screen reader users.
claims.quote:
The help links to HMRC open in a new tab. Their visible text is unchanged
  and a visually hidden "(opens in a new tab)" tells screen reader users.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the customs link goes to HMRC's customs, international trade and excise enquiries page rather than its contact index, which lists every tax and helpline.

The customs link goes to HMRC's customs, international trade and excise
  enquiries page, not its contact index, which lists every tax and helpline.

"Create a new notification" is a form button styled as a link, because

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the declaration's confirmation is one small checkbox in a fieldset whose legend is for screen readers only, so a lone checkbox still has a group label.

The confirmation is one small checkbox in a fieldset whose legend is for

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the declaration page carries no status strip, at a first submission or an amendment.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the date of declaration is shown in bold.
claims.quote: The date of declaration is shown in bold.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that a hidden step field tells a Submit from a Continue on the declaration, because an unticked box posts nothing.
claims.quote:
The hidden `step` tells a Submit from a Continue, because an unticked box
  posts nothing.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the declaration checkbox is never pre-ticked, because a tick left by a submit refused as stale was given to older content.

The checkbox is never pre-ticked, because a tick left by a submit refused

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the country of origin is required on save and continue, an empty answer being refused with "Select a country of origin", a typed value not in the list with "Select a country from the list", and a saved country the reference data no longer offers being refused on submit with its own message.
claims.quote:
The country is required on save and continue. An empty answer is refused with
  **Select a country of origin**; a typed value not in the list is refused with
  **Select a country from the list**. A saved country the reference data no
  longer offers is refused on submit with its own message.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the country of origin list names a territory with its country, as in "Canary Islands (Spain)", and is sorted by the name shown.
claims.quote:
The list names a territory with its country, "Canary Islands (Spain)", and
  is sorted by the name shown.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that with JavaScript the region code box shows the country's code as a fixed prefix, empty until a country is picked and filled in as soon as one is so the trader types only the rest, that without JavaScript there is no prefix, and that the stored answer is the whole joined code either way.
claims.quote:
With JavaScript the region code box shows the country's code as a fixed
  prefix, empty until a country is picked and filled in as soon as one is, so
  the trader types only the rest. Without JavaScript there is no prefix. The
  stored answer is the whole joined code either way.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the server always draws the region code prefix so a revisit or an error shows the saved or submitted code at once, styling hiding it until GOV.UK Frontend's JavaScript can run and a small client module updating it on a change of country.
claims.quote:
The server always draws the prefix, so a revisit or an error shows the saved
  or submitted code at once. Styling hides it until GOV.UK Frontend's
  JavaScript can run, and a small client module updates it on a change of
  country.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the country-to-prefix rule has one owner on the server, the page handing the browser a map built with it and the client module only looking the chosen country up.
claims.quote:
The country-to-prefix rule has one owner on the server. The page hands the
  browser a map built with it, and the module only looks the chosen country up.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that a region code typed with the country's code and a hyphen, such as FR-75, is recognised and not doubled, while a code typed with the country's letters but no hyphen, such as FR75, is kept as typed and joined to the prefix as FR-FR75, because a real region code can begin with those letters.
claims.quote:
A code typed with the country's code and a hyphen (for example "FR-75") is
  recognised and not doubled. A code typed with the country's letters but no
  hyphen (for example "FR75") is kept as typed and joined to the prefix
  ("FR-FR75"), because a real region code can begin with those letters.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the region code is required under Yes and stored only with a country's prefix, and that under No, or with no country, the stored code is empty.
claims.quote:
The region code is required under Yes, and stored only with a country's
  prefix. Under No, or with no country, the stored code is empty.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the region code rules measure the typed part with any typed prefix removed, whatever the answer, while the page shows back what was typed.
claims.quote:
The rules measure the typed part with any typed prefix removed, whatever the
  answer; the page shows back what was typed.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the region code box stops typing at the same length the rule allows, the stop applying to the raw text, so a trader without JavaScript who types the country's code before a rest of more than two characters has it cut short.
claims.quote:
The region code box stops typing at the same length the rule allows. The
  stop applies to the raw text, so a trader without JavaScript who types the
  country's code before a rest of more than two characters has it cut short.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that clearing the country clears the region code too, because the prefix depends on the country.
claims.quote:
Clearing the country clears the region code too, because the prefix
  depends on the country.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the internal reference is checked for length only, being the trader's own and keeping their punctuation.
claims.quote:
The internal reference is checked for length only. It is the trader's own
  and keeps their punctuation.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the origin page's status strip shows from the first request.
claims.quote: The status strip shows from the first request.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that stored answers are re-checked against the origin page's rules when the page opens, so a country the reference data no longer offers is named on the page.
claims.quote:
Stored answers are re-checked against the page's rules when the page opens,

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the Overview origin task reads Complete only when a country is chosen and the region of origin code question is answered, Yes with a code or No.
claims.quote:
The overview origin task reads Complete only when a country is chosen and
  the region of origin code question is answered (Yes with a code, or No).

claims.statement: The page-design record states that a question two import reasons ask has a form field per reason because two inputs cannot share a name, both mapping back to the one answer.
claims.quote:
A question two reasons ask has a form field per reason, because two inputs

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the reason a reveal belongs to carries the explanation, so its follow-up questions ask with a label alone and the exit date keeps only its worked example.
claims.quote:
The reason a reveal belongs to carries the explanation, so its follow-up

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the unreadable-date message does not repeat the field name the label already gives.
claims.quote:
The unreadable-date message does not repeat the field name that the label

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the destination country and port of exit are type-ahead searches using the shared search control, with the look the origin and port of entry searches share: a bold label and full width.
claims.quote:
The destination country and port of exit are type-ahead searches using the

  share: a bold label and full width.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that type-ahead suggestions match ignoring accents as well as case, so plain letters find "Côte d'Ivoire".
claims.quote:
Type-ahead suggestions match ignoring accents as well as case, so plain

claims.statement: The page-design record states that origin and port of entry share the medium label while the main import reason page asks its searches as follow-up questions, so it sets the small label itself and "Select one" in both the empty box and the select's first option.
claims.quote:
Origin and port of entry share the medium label, but this page asks its
  searches as follow-up questions, so it sets the small label itself, and
  "Select one" in both the empty box and the select's first option.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the exit date has a regular-weight label and a GOV.UK margin override on its form group, because GOV.UK Frontend zeroes the bottom margin of the last form group nested in another, which would leave the date box touching "Port of exit".
claims.quote:
The exit date has a regular-weight label and a GOV.UK margin override on its
  form group. GOV.UK Frontend zeroes
  the bottom margin of the last form group nested in another, which would leave
  the date box touching "Port of exit".

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the additional details page's certification hint names the ITAHC because a trader holds several certificates so "the health certificate" does not say which one the certification purposes are copied from, the abbreviation matching the documents and review pages.
claims.quote:
The certification hint names the ITAHC because a trader holds several
  certificates, so "the health certificate" does not say which one the
  certification purposes are copied from. The abbreviation matches the
  documents and review pages.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the identification page uses the full-width surface so the tables and cards fit, while the error summary, caption, heading and inset text keep a two-thirds reading width.
claims.quote:
The page uses the full-width surface so the tables and cards fit. The error
  summary, caption, heading and inset text keep a two-thirds reading width.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that identification is grouped by commodity, one section per commodity headed "<commodity name> (<commodity code>)" holding one card per species.
claims.quote:
Identification is grouped by commodity: one section per commodity headed
  "<commodity name> (<commodity code>)", holding one card per species.

claims.statement: The page-design record states the decision that the identification card is built from GOV.UK summary card styling and govukTable rather than the prototype's custom CSS and div grid, so tables keep their meaning and reflow at 390px.

The

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the saved-animals and Selected commodities tables set a deliberate custom class on their cells so long unbroken identifiers and commodity names wrap inside table cells at 390px.

The saved-animals and Selected commodities tables set

claims.statement: The page-design record states that a species with no number of animals has no identification card, and a consignment whose species all lack a count shows the summary and no cards.
claims.quote:
A species with no number of animals has no card, and a consignment whose
  species all lack a count shows the summary and no cards.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the identification card title is the species name with "Change number of animals" beside it naming the species, and that the link pushes the identification page onto the trail so Back on the count page returns there and Continue on Commodity details goes on to the next page that applies.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that while animals remain the identification card shows the entry form, then the in-card button, then the saved-animals table, that a finished species shows its saved animals alone with no form, no button and no completion message, and that a count lowered below its saved records still shows the over-count message.
claims.quote:
While animals remain the card shows the entry form, then the in-card button,
  then the saved-animals table. A finished species shows its saved animals
  alone, with no form, no button and no completion message. A count lowered
  below its saved records still shows the over-count message.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the identification in-card button says what pressing it does next, reading "Save and add another" while more than one animal is outstanding and "Save and finish" on the last, is a primary button, saves only its own species' current animal and reloads with that form empty, and that a line of one animal has no in-card button.
claims.quote:
The in-card button says what pressing it does next: "Save and add another"
  while more than one animal is outstanding, "Save and finish" on the last,

  and reloads with that form empty. A line of one animal has no in-card

claims.statement: The page-design record states that on the identification page "Save and continue" and "Save and return to overview" save only the forms of species with one animal, values typed into the form of a species with more animals being neither validated nor saved by them.
claims.quote:
"Save and continue" and "Save and return to overview"
  save only the forms of species with one animal. Values typed into the form
  of a species with more animals are neither validated nor saved by them.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that pressing Enter in any identification field presses the page's hidden default button, which saves every card holding typed values including species with more animals and keeps the trader on the page when one of those was saved, the hidden button coming first in the form so Enter never presses a Remove button or the visible "Save and continue".
claims.quote:
Pressing Enter in any field presses the page's hidden default button. It
  saves every card holding typed values, species with more animals included,
  and keeps the trader on the page when one of those was saved. The hidden
  button comes first in the form so that Enter never presses a Remove button

claims.statement: The page-design record states that an identifier has one name used both on the entry field and as the saved-animals column heading, that no identifier field has a hint, and that the labels are regular weight.
claims.quote:
An identifier has one name, used both on the entry field and as the
  saved-animals column heading, and no identifier field has a hint. Labels
  are regular weight.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the saved-animals table has one column per identifier that species' panel asks for rather than per identifier the trader filled — the commodity's own identifiers, or the two free-text fallback answers for a commodity that declares none — so the header row says which identifiers the line expects and an empty cell shows which are still missing.
claims.quote:
The saved-animals table has one column per identifier that species' panel

  identifiers, or the two free-text fallback answers for a commodity that
  declares none. The header row says which identifiers the line expects, and

claims.statement: The page-design record states that removing an identifier record is a POST on the card form with no GET, so a link cannot trigger it.
claims.quote:
Removing an identifier record is a POST on the card form with no GET, so a
  link cannot trigger it.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the identification page is skipped only when the notification holds no commodity line.
claims.quote: The page is skipped only when the notification holds no commodity line.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that on the commodity pages a choice made under an earlier search has no tick box on screen, so it is sent back with the form as a hidden value.
claims.quote:
A choice made under an earlier search has no tick box on screen, so it is
  sent back with the form as a hidden value.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that with JavaScript the commodity search results refresh in place as the trader types, ticks, removes or clears, through the shared multi-select search, and that the results are the ones the page renders without JavaScript so the ordering, labelling and selection rules hold on both paths.
claims.quote:
With JavaScript the results refresh in place as the trader types, ticks,

claims.statement: The page-design record states that a polite status message gives the number of species a typed commodity search lists, or "No results found", and that a tick, a Remove or Clear all is not announced because the box and the tally already show it.
claims.quote:
A polite status message gives the number of species a typed
  search lists, or "No results found". A tick, a Remove or Clear all is not
  announced, because the box and the tally already show it.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that after a Remove or Clear all on the commodity search the button pressed has gone so focus moves to the search box, while after a tick focus stays on the tick box.

After a Remove or Clear all, the button pressed has gone, so focus moves to
  the search box. After a tick, focus stays on the tick box.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that without JavaScript a tick cannot refresh the tally so an "Add selection" secondary button sits under the commodity results, running the search again keeping the term and the ticks so the tally catches up, and that with JavaScript the button is hidden.
claims.quote:
Without JavaScript a tick cannot refresh the tally, so an "Add selection"
  secondary button sits under the results. It runs the search again, keeping
  the term and the ticks, and the tally catches up. With JavaScript
  the button is hidden, because a tick refreshes the tally itself.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the "Add selection" button and its copy are agreed for now and will be revisited when the designers pick up their no-JavaScript ticket.

The button and
  its copy are agreed for now, and will be revisited when the designers pick
  up their no-JavaScript ticket.
claims.note: The only place the repo records a piece of English copy as provisionally agreed and awaiting a design decision.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that the commodity search results are a list joined to the bottom of the search box as the design draws it: one heading row per commodity with its species beneath, striped rows ruled the full width of the list with the first species under each heading shaded, no ring round a hovered tick box, and a scroll once the list is taller than about six rows.

The results are a list joined to the bottom of the search box, as the

  rows ruled the full width of the list (the first species under each heading
  shaded), no ring round a hovered tick box, and a scroll once the list is taller

claims.statement: The page-design record states that each commodity in the search results stays a fieldset whose legend is its heading, so a screen reader hears the species grouped by commodity.
claims.quote:
Each commodity stays a fieldset whose legend is its
  heading, so a screen reader hears the species grouped by commodity.

claims.statement: The page-design record states that a commodity's heading in the results and in the tally reads as its name with its code in round brackets, such as "Cattle (0102)", where the service knows a name for the code, and as the code alone where it does not, while the Commodity details page still names a commodity by its code.
claims.quote:
A commodity's heading in the results, and in the tally, reads as
  its name with its code in round brackets, such as "Cattle (0102)", where the
  service knows a name for the code, and as the code alone where it does not.

claims.quote:
With JavaScript, Escape in the search box or a click outside the search hides
  the list, keeping the term and every choice, and focusing or clicking the
